dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName="ConsoleLogin" responseElements.ConsoleLogin="Success"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.5_console_login_without_mf_5"
| sort -_time
description: Console access without MFA is a security risk — compromised passwords alone can grant full account access. Most compliance frameworks require MFA.
value: Detecting console login without mfa early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Monitor ConsoleLogin events. Alert on successful console logins where MFA is not used. Exclude service accounts that authenticate via SSO (which has its own MFA).
visualization: Table (user, source IP, MFA status), Pie chart (MFA vs. no-MFA), Single value.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
  where Authentication.action="success" AND (match(Authentication.signature, "(?i)ConsoleLogin|AwsConsoleSignIn") OR match(Authentication.app, "(?i)signin\\.amazonaws"))
  AND NOT (Authentication.mfa="true" OR lower(Authentication.authentication_method)="mfa")
  by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.app span=1h
| sort -count

knownFalsePositives: Federated SSO through SAML or OIDC that enforces MFA at the IdP, so the AWS record may not show the same second factor detail.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Monitor ConsoleLogin events. Alert on successful console logins where MFA is not used. Exclude service accounts that authenticate via SSO (which has its own MFA).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName="ConsoleLogin" responseElements.ConsoleLogin="Success"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.5_console_login_without_mf_5"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect console login without mfa. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_5_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (user, source IP, MFA status), Pie chart (MFA vs. no-MFA), Single value..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of console login without mfa so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
